name: LASER: LLM Agent with State-Space Exploration for Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LASER represents web navigation as exploration over a defined set of states, allowing an agent to revisit earlier states after mistakes. The study evaluates this backtracking approach on WebShop and Amazon tasks.

name: Exposing Limitations of Language Model Agents in Sequential-Task Compositions on the Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CompWoB adds 50 composed web-automation tasks to study generalization from simpler interactions. The paper compares prompted and fine-tuned agents, balances task training data, and probes sensitivity to changes in instruction order.

name: A Trembling House of Cards? Mapping Adversarial Attacks against Language Agents
notes: Adjacent conceptual security work: the paper describes hypothetical scenarios and a future generalist agent. Scope was checked against the retained abstract and full-text Sections 2.4 and 3.
summary: Presents a conceptual perception–reasoning–action framework and 12 potential attack scenarios for language agents, including hypothetical web-navigation attacks.

name: PPTC-R benchmark: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models for PowerPoint Task Completion
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. The benchmark directly concerns PowerPoint task automation but executes through APIs, so it remains adjacent.
summary: Benchmarks robustness of API-based PowerPoint completion under sentence-level, semantic, and multilingual instruction perturbations and changes to the available API set.

name: WILBUR: Adaptive In-Context Learning for Robust and Accurate Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WILBUR learns to rank prior task demonstrations for a web agent’s prompt and synthesizes instructions from past runs. A generated task curriculum and a backtracking mechanism support adaptation and recovery, evaluated on WebVoyager.

name: Benchmarking Mobile Device Control Agents across Diverse Configurations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces B-MoCA, an interactive mobile-control benchmark that varies device settings, layouts, and languages to test generalization.

name: Dynamic Planning for LLM-based Graphical User Interface Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Dynamic Planning of Thoughts revises a mobile GUI plan using current environmental feedback and execution history. The study compares this planning strategy with long-dialogue prompting and examines its behavior on unfamiliar tasks and different language-model backbones.

name: Multimodal Auto Validation For Self-Refinement in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies text and visual validation for web agents and uses the resulting validator to detect failures and guide workflow self-refinement.

name: OSCAR: Operating System Control via State-Aware Reasoning and Re-Planning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSCAR translates user instructions into Python control code while observing screen images and acting through mouse and keyboard operations. A state-machine controller handles errors and replans tasks during execution across desktop and mobile applications.

name: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. The full paper was also inspected to confirm WebShop evaluation; the broader agent-learning method is classified as adjacent.
summary: Builds self-critique training examples from searched recovery paths to improve agents' ability to detect and correct errors during interaction.

name: WorldGUI: An Interactive Benchmark for Desktop GUI Automation from Any Starting Point
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces desktop and web tasks with varied initial states to test planning recovery and adaptability beyond canonical starting configurations.

name: Evaluating the Robustness of Multimodal Agents Against Active Environmental Injection Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Examines active environmental injection against mobile agents, testing whether adversarial interface content redirects decisions during task execution.

name: Advancing Language Multi-Agent Learning with Credit Re-Assignment for Interactive Environment Generalization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces CollabUIAgents, a multi-agent RL framework that assigns LLM-based process rewards to help agents generalize across interactive settings including mobile operations and web browsing.

name: On the Robustness of GUI Grounding Models Against Image Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates GUI grounding models under natural image noise, untargeted adversarial perturbations, and targeted image attacks. Experiments cover mobile, desktop, and web interfaces and analyze sensitivity to image resolution and adversarial changes.

name: WebRollback: Enhancing Web Agents with Explicit Rollback Mechanisms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebRollback gives a web agent an explicit action for returning to an earlier state in its navigation trajectory. It studies this recovery mechanism on two live web-navigation benchmarks under both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings.

name: Mobile-Bench-v2: A More Realistic and Comprehensive Benchmark for VLM-based Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Mobile-Bench-v2 evaluates mobile GUI agents using multiple acceptable offline action paths, noisy interfaces with ads or pop-ups, and ambiguous instructions with scripted clarification exchanges. These splits separate step-level execution, robustness, and proactive interaction.

name: GEM: Gaussian Embedding Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Detection in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GEM detects instructions outside a GUI agent’s capabilities by modeling distances in its input-embedding space with a Gaussian mixture. Experiments across mobile, computer and browser data also examine selective escalation to a cloud model when an input is detected as unfamiliar.

name: TransBench: Breaking Barriers for Transferable Graphical User Interface Agents in Dynamic Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces TransBench to evaluate GUI grounding transfer across app versions, iOS, Android, Web, and functionally distinct applications.

name: BacktrackAgent: Enhancing GUI Agent with Error Detection and Backtracking Mechanism
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BacktrackAgent adds verification, judgment, and reflection modules to detect erroneous GUI actions and guide recovery. It develops backtracking-oriented training data that includes post-action pages and evaluates task completion and step accuracy on Mobile3M and Auto-UI.

name: UI-Evol: Automatic Knowledge Evolving for Computer Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UI-Evol, which extracts action sequences from agent interactions and critiques external guidance against those traces. Evaluation on OSWorld examines how revised operational knowledge affects execution and behavioral consistency.

name: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained paper abstract; Android setup is supported separately by the official project README.
summary: Benchmarks truthfulness, controllability, safety, and privacy of multimodal LLM agents across interactive web and mobile GUI tasks.

name: Look Before You Leap: A GUI-Critic-R1 Model for Pre-Operative Error Diagnosis in GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses a pre-execution critic and reinforcement training to evaluate proposed GUI actions and provide corrective suggestions before execution.

name: GUIPilot: A Consistency-based Mobile GUI Testing Approach for Detecting Application-specific Bugs
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces GUIPilot, which compares mobile design mock-ups with implemented screens through widget alignment and tests expected transitions by executing inferred UI actions. It evaluates both visual inconsistencies and workflow-specific bugs.

name: GUI-Reflection: Empowering Multimodal GUI Models with Self-Reflection Behavior
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-Reflection synthesizes reflection and error-correction examples from successful trajectories and adds dedicated learning stages for these behaviors. It introduces a reflection task suite, a mobile environment for online data collection, and iterative reflection tuning.

name: Poison Once, Control Anywhere: Clean-Text Visual Backdoors in VLM-based Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Demonstrates clean-text visual backdoor attacks (VIBMA) that compromise fine-tuned VLM mobile agents through visual triggers while keeping text instructions intact.

name: GUI-Robust: A Comprehensive Dataset for Testing GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds GUI task data with real-world interaction anomalies and evaluates how agent behavior changes under those conditions.

name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.

name: MobileUse: A GUI Agent with Hierarchical Reflection for Autonomous Mobile Operation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileUse reflects on errors at action and task timescales, invoking reflection when needed and using proactive exploration to learn unfamiliar apps. It evaluates this mobile execution framework on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab and describes a toolkit for physical-device operation.

name: NaviMaster: Learning a Unified Policy for GUI and Embodied Navigation Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: NaviMaster trains a shared policy for GUI and embodied navigation using a common visual-trajectory formulation. It combines trajectory collection, reinforcement learning and distance-aware rewards, with evaluation across both task families.

name: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Chameleon, an environmental-injection evaluation framework that varies webpage content and trigger context. It combines simulated page variation with attention-based optimization and tests GUI agents across realistic websites.

name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.

name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.

name: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on web interface reasoning, visual perturbation robustness, and safety-critical web understanding tasks.

name: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The reported contribution evaluates attack detection.
summary: Introduces WAInjectBench with a threat-model taxonomy and malicious and benign text-image datasets for web-agent prompt-injection detection. It compares detector families across explicit and less visible forms of injected content.

name: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.

name: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.

name: Invisible to Humans, Triggered by Agents: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Mobile Vision-Language Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses the near-zero contact-touch signals of automated mobile agents to expose malicious visual content selectively during agent interactions. The paper combines this agent-only perceptual injection with HG-IDA* prompt optimization to study unauthorized cross-app actions.

name: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SecureWebArena with simulated interactive websites, an attack-vector taxonomy and labeled agent trajectories. Its evaluation separates failures in reasoning, behavioral traces and task outcomes across vision-language agent families.

name: Surfer 2: The Next Generation of Cross-Platform Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.

name: D-GARA: A Dynamic Benchmarking Framework for GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: D-GARA evaluates Android GUI agents under runtime anomalies such as permission dialogs, battery warnings, and update prompts. Its modular environment embeds these interruptions in Android applications to study recovery and robustness.

name: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-CUBE evaluates 226 tasks ranging from individual controls to copy-paste and enterprise workflows. Interface variations, multiple resolutions, and application-state validation support diagnosis of operational reliability beyond task accuracy alone.

name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.

name: MPR-GUI: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multilingual Perception and Reasoning in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MPR-GUI evaluates GUI perception and reasoning through strictly aligned tasks in six languages. GUI-XLI adjusts non-English hidden representations toward English representations at language-sensitive layers during inference to address the measured cross-language gaps.

name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.

name: MVP: Multiple View Prediction Improves GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.

name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.

name: AndroidLens: Long-latency Evaluation with Nested Sub-targets for Android GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AndroidLens provides 571 extended mobile tasks in Chinese and English, with multiple valid paths and preserved environmental anomalies. Its dynamic evaluation uses nested milestones and Average Task Progress to measure partial completion of long workflows.

name: Agent-Dice: Disentangling Knowledge Updates via Geometric Consensus for Agent Continual Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). GUI agents are one of the domains used to evaluate this general continual-learning method.
summary: Agent-Dice fuses parameter updates to support continual learning in LLM agents, with GUI agent tasks evaluated alongside tool-use domains.

name: When Bots Take the Bait: Exposing and Mitigating the Emerging Social Engineering Attack in Web Automation Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies deceptive social-engineering web patterns targeting browser automation agents and proposes defenses against bait-based manipulation.

name: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: NOVA separates trusted task planning from screen-derived observations by producing a branching plan before execution and resolving runtime values through perception. Its OSWorld study examines security and utility while identifying remaining risks from perception-driven branch steering.

name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.

name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.

name: MobileBench-OL: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Mobile GUI Agents in Real-World Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MobileBench-OL, an online benchmark of Chinese-app tasks spanning execution, reasoning, exploration, and noisy conditions. Its automatic evaluation and reset framework supports repeated testing of mobile GUI agents in real environments.

name: Continual GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.

name: BEAP-Agent: Backtrackable Execution and Adaptive Planning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: BEAP-Agent treats GUI execution as depth-first search with coordinated planning, execution and task-state tracking. It supports backtracking across multiple levels of earlier states and evaluates recovery on OSWorld.

name: SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SafeGround, which estimates GUI-grounding uncertainty from the spatial dispersion of sampled predictions and calibrates a decision threshold before testing. It studies risk-aware selection on ScreenSpot-Pro, with statistical control scoped to the threshold’s false-discovery rate.

name: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: MisActBench provides action-level labels for task alignment, while DeAction checks proposed computer-use actions and requests revisions through structured feedback. The paper separately evaluates offline detection and interactive operation in OSWorld and RedTeamCUA.

name: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: ACuRL uses autonomous interface exploration and an adaptive task curriculum to continually train computer-use policies with reinforcement learning. CUAJudge supplies outcome feedback, and experiments study adaptation across desktop applications and environment changes.

name: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as future work.
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning for continual GUI learning, using policy entropy to adjust their proportions and gradient projection to limit conflicting updates. AndroidControl-CL groups applications into sequential tasks to evaluate adaptation and retention.

name: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TimeWarp tests web agents across multiple versions of the same sites, varying visual design, frontend code and workflows. TimeTraj transfers plans across versions to collect training trajectories and study robustness to interface change.

name: Generalization in Online Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroidWorld-Generalization with separate tests for unseen task instances, templates, and applications. A GRPO training system combines containerized environments with asynchronous trajectory collection to study these generalization regimes.

name: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUAAudit examines vision-language models that judge computer-use task completion from an instruction and final environment state. Across macOS, Windows and Linux benchmarks, it measures accuracy, confidence calibration and disagreement between auditors.

name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.

name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.

name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.

name: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract limits its portability evidence to transfer within a benchmark family.
summary: Turns draft web-agent skills into structured executable artifacts that support deterministic checks, fault localization and local repair. VisualWebArena and MiniWoB experiments examine execution and reuse within the same benchmark family.

name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.

name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.

name: Don't Act Blindly: Robust GUI Automation via Action-Effect Verification and Self-Correction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces VeriGUI, which checks expected action effects and reasons about recovery before subsequent GUI actions. Training combines synthetic failure trajectories with verification-weighted GRPO, evaluated on an AndroidControl-based robustness benchmark.

name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.

name: PrecisionCUA: Iterative Visual Refinement for Pixel-Precise Cursor Grounding in Code Editors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies iterative cursor grounding in dense code-editor interfaces, using visual feedback from earlier attempts to correct displacement. PrecisionCUA evaluates this closed-loop process across multiple model families on coding-interface tasks.

name: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Perturbed, which varies screenshot appearance and instruction wording independently to diagnose grounding failures. Experiments on three related model architectures examine relational instructions, browser zoom and augmentation-based fine-tuning.

name: FedGUI: Benchmarking Federated GUI Agents across Heterogeneous Platforms, Devices, and Operating Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces FedGUI, a federated GUI-learning benchmark built from six datasets spanning mobile, web and desktop interfaces. Its experiments separate platform, device, operating-system and data-source heterogeneity when evaluating collaborative training.

name: StressWeb: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Web Agent Robustness under Realistic Interaction Variability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The tests use constructed, controllable web environments with clean workflows as baselines.
summary: Introduces a web-agent stress-testing benchmark with controlled changes to layouts, interaction semantics, and execution for diagnosing behavior under varied conditions.

name: Penny Wise, Pixel Foolish: Bypassing Price Constraints in Multimodal Agents via Visual Adversarial Perturbations
notes: Scope is screenshot-based interface understanding and safety. The retained abstract leaves the operating system and live transaction execution unspecified.
summary: Introduces PriceBlind, a visual perturbation method for controlled screenshot-based evaluation of price-constrained multimodal agents. The reported transfer experiments use a simplified single-turn coordinate-selection protocol.

name: HalluClear: Diagnosing, Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucinations in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HalluClear with a GUI hallucination taxonomy, expert-calibrated evaluation workflow and structured-reasoning post-training scheme. It evaluates how these components affect hallucinations, grounding and action fidelity across GUI agents.

name: Do LLMs Need to See Everything? A Benchmark and Study of Failures in LLM-driven Smartphone Automation using Screentext vs. Screenshots
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DailyDroid compares text-only and text-plus-screenshot agents on everyday Android tasks across multiple apps and difficulty levels. Its failure analysis examines accessibility, observation modality and agent/application behavior.

name: WebUncertainty: Dual-Level Uncertainty Driven Planning and Reasoning For Autonomous Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebUncertainty adapts planning mode to task uncertainty and guides action-level tree search with confidence-derived uncertainty estimates. Its evaluations examine autonomous execution of dynamic, long-horizon web tasks on WebArena and WebVoyager.

name: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study examines repeated OSWorld executions to separate execution stochasticity, task-specification ambiguity and behavioral variation. Paired task-level tests show why one successful run is insufficient evidence of reliable computer use.

name: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study examines UI changes between a desktop agent’s screenshot observation and action dispatch. Its pre-execution state checks address overlay and focus manipulation, while the reported DOM-injection blind spot limits the defense’s coverage.

name: VLAA-GUI: Knowing When to Stop, Recover, and Search, A Modular Framework for GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VLAA-GUI combines mandatory checks for visually supported completion, multi-tier loop recovery and on-demand workflow search. Optional coding and grounding agents support execution, with component ablations on Linux and Windows GUI tasks.

name: OS-SPEAR: A Toolkit for the Safety, Performance,Efficiency, and Robustness Analysis of OS Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Provides an evaluation toolkit for joint safety, efficiency, and multimodal robustness analysis of operating-system GUI agents.

name: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

Site data is downloaded from the Hugging Face dataset sparklabutah/timewarp-env-data. src/browsergym/timewarp registers timewarp.1 to timewarp.231 with BrowserGym; its task file has 231 tasks: 70 Wiki-only, 64 Shop-only, 47 News-only and 50 spanning two or three sites. Agents answer in free text, which is normalized and checked by string_match, number_match and list_match verifiers (AND-combined per task); 2 tasks use only the LLM judge (GPT-5 by default, or a locally served Gemma model). scripts/ runs AgentLab studies per site and sweeps models and UI versions; collectTeacherTraj/ provides a modified AgentLab loop and agent that save teacher trajectories, llamafactory/ has full and LoRA fine-tuning configs for training on them, and the README points to GPT-5 traces on Hugging Face. scripts/annotation holds the verifier authoring and audit tooling, results/ has page-measurement and visual-information validation data, and proofs/ has Lean 4 proofs of the appendix theory. The README shows an MIT badge without a link, and the tree has no root license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release.
summary: Web-agent benchmark on self-hosted Wiki, News and Shop sites, each with six era-styled UI versions, registering 231 BrowserGym tasks scored mainly by deterministic answer verifiers.

name: CloudCruise
notes: The homepage targets payer-portal and EHR workflows and says every run executes in a VM with laptop-like fingerprints and human-like input, with queued concurrency, video replay, per-action screenshots and logs, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. The documentation says the builder agent opens a live browser preview, navigates the target site, asks clarifying questions and turns confirmed actions into a node-and-edge graph that later runs deterministically, with model calls confined to building the graph. Click nodes target elements either by XPath or through an LLM vision mode labelled AI (Screenshot). The maintenance agent classifies failures from the error screenshot, page state and selector signals, then recovers in place, asks for input, retries or hands the workflow to the builder agent. Citrix virtual desktops are automated through their HTML5 browser client using the screenshot mode. Runs start through an API with TypeScript and Python SDKs.
summary: Managed browser-automation platform for healthcare portals and EHRs in which a builder agent turns a chat description into a reusable workflow graph that runs in cloud VMs and a maintenance agent repairs.
